items.stem: Under the accruals (matching) concept, how should rent paid in advance for the next accounting period be treated at the year end?

options.text: Carried forward as a prepayment (current asset)
options.rationale: Correct: rent relating to a future period is a prepayment and is carried forward as an asset.

options.text: Charged in full to this year's profit or loss
options.rationale: Charging it all this year breaches the matching concept.
It has been paid, so it is not a liability; it is a prepaid asset.
The accruals concept requires recognising the prepayment now.

items.explanation: Correct: rent relating to a future period is a prepayment and is carried forward as an asset.

items.stem: A receivables ledger control account is used primarily to:

options.text: Provide a total check on the individual customer accounts in the receivables ledger
options.rationale: Correct: the control account's balance should agree with the sum of the individual receivable balances, giving a control check.
Cash sales do not create receivables; the control account summarises credit customers.

options.text: Replace the need for individual customer accounts
options.rationale: Individual accounts are still kept; the control account summarises them.
Depreciation is unrelated to the receivables control account.

items.explanation: Correct: the control account's balance should agree with the sum of the individual receivable balances, giving a control check.
